learning: Lowering base_speed from 1.6 to 1.2 raised the score with geometry unchanged, which suggests the excursion depends partly on speed. Whether this holds on an unseen track is untested.
notes: Final package: iteration-2 geometry with the iteration-10 controller (base_speed 1.2, the best-scoring pairing at 27.3854). No further iteration follows, so the package is not tuned beyond the evidence.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so this package races the unseen final track with no later correction. The geometry is the iteration-2 row, which the Geometry Builder asked me to hold: five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.05 to +0.05 m, y = 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.18 m, mass 0.8 kg. Across eleven raced designs, span is the only geometry lever that changed line loss (iteration 1 removed it on oval and slalom). Footprint, wheel_track (0.10 and 0.15 m), mass, wheel_radius, and sensor y (0.02, 0.04, 0.06 m) all left max_error at about 0.061 m, so I have no evidence for a geometry change. The controller is the iteration-10 controller, which is the best-scoring pairing so far (27.3854). It keeps kp 3.5, ki 0, kd 0.05, last_direction recovery and weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1], and lowers base_speed from 1.6 to 1.2. Iteration 10 raised the score by about 0.39 with the same geometry, and oval max_error moved only slightly. Two cautions apply. First, iteration 9 showed that kd 0.15 gave identical results, so kd stays at 0.05. Second, base_speed was tested only at 1.2 and 1.6, so I do not extrapolate below 1.2. Expected result, not measured: the same behaviour as iteration 10, with zero line loss and max_error near 0.061 m on the development tracks. The score on the unseen track is not predicted.
